analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml:169 opts into scoped responses; :196-202 derives the exact expected profile/optional-size/run-ID label locally. The existing exact-array comparison at :207 and fallback at :211-213 reject generic or different-run responses rather than widening runner eligibility. Run identity comes from GitHub context (:54-55), with numeric validation before requests (:154-160); plane data is not interpolated as executable shell. Fork exclusion, empty permissions, HTTPS transport bounds, lane caps and output sanitization remain unchanged. No concrete security regression was identified.

changelog.d/ci-run-isolation.md:3 and docs/developer/build.md patch head :492-501 describe this narrowing consistently. This is CI scheduling isolation, not provider serving authorization, attestation, encryption or cache isolation; no supplied change alters A-001/A-003, T-041, T-053 or T-054 controls. Build integrity remains relevant to A-017, but labels alone do not authenticate runner provenance.

Integration must verify the sandbox plane/provisioner contract: the header must produce matching scoped labels on actual registered runners, with sufficient lifetime for queued jobs and individual-job retries. That implementation and unchanged workflow callers/tests are not supplied. Unsupported replies visibly fall back, so absent external evidence does not establish a vulnerability; an accepted scoped response without a matching live runner could instead strand jobs. The run ID intentionally excludes attempt identity, so the claim covers distinct workflow runs, not isolation between attempts of one run. Remaining uncertainty concerns end-to-end provisioning and availability, not an observed missing client control.
